agency_or_partner: North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources (DNCR), Office of the Secretary
public_problem: DNCR manages many natural and cultural sites and programs across North Carolina but does not have a comprehensive assessment of their economic impact on the state and on local communities.
why_it_matters: DNCR wants evidence to support continued investment, strategic budget requests to the General Assembly, fundraising, marketing decisions, and decisions about how its sites and programs contribute to local economies, especially rural communities.
target_population: North Carolina communities served by DNCR sites and programs; rural communities are specifically mentioned as important. Specific visitor demographics are not yet collected across the board.
available_data: Monthly visitation data reported by DNCR sites
Latitude and longitude for site locations
Grant awards by program and county through a Power BI dashboard
VisitNC county tourism data that can be linked to site locations
Existing economic impact reports for aquariums, the zoo, state parks, and related arts economy examples
Potential procurement data including purchase amount, vendor, and vendor zip code, but availability is not fully confirmed
Hub spend data for historically underutilized businesses
Planned visitor survey data from Memorial Day to Labor Day
expected_outputs: A statewide top-line assessment of DNCR's economic impact
More detailed individual reports for DNCR sites
Measures such as economic output, jobs supported, visitor spending, and local and state tax revenue
Possibly analysis of programs and grant programs, but this is described as a nice-to-have rather than a must-have
Feedback on survey design and data collection approach before summer deployment
timeline: DNCR wants survey design decisions relatively quickly
Visitor survey planned from Memorial Day to Labor Day
Specific final project deadline unclear from transcript
stakeholders: David Yokum, Office of State Budget and Management
DNCR divisions including state parks, aquariums, museums, historic sites, the zoo, libraries, arts-related programs, and grant programs
General Assembly and other budget or funding decision makers
Local communities affected by DNCR sites and programs
student_entry_points: Clean and organize visitation, site, grant, or survey data
Compare data collection methods across sites
Link site location data to county tourism or demographic data
Help design or test visitor survey questions
Create exploratory charts, maps, or dashboard mockups
Review existing economic impact reports and summarize reusable methods
Document uncertainty, missing fields, and data quality issues
researcher_opportunities: Design an economic impact methodology suitable for DNCR's varied sites and programs
Estimate statewide and local economic impact of DNCR sites
Advise on visitor survey design, sampling, timing, and collection tools
Assess how procurement and vendor geography affect in-state economic impact
Determine whether program and grant impacts can be estimated in addition to physical site impacts
Evaluate feasibility risks caused by inconsistent visitation methods and missing demographic data

important_quotes_or_evidence: DNCR has a question about how the economic impact of their different sites and programs can be estimated.
DNCR has over 100 sites across North Carolina.
DNCR sites are described as economic anchors for many North Carolina communities, particularly rural communities.
They have never assessed, to their knowledge, a comprehensive look at the economic impact for these places in the state.
The minimum viable product includes a larger top-line assessment and more detailed individual reports.
The must-have is sites; programs are described as more of a nice-to-have.
DNCR has monthly visitation data, operational budgets, site latitude and longitude, grant data by program and county, and VisitNC county tourism data.
DNCR does not currently collect demographic information across the board.
DNCR plans to deploy a survey from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
